additions.text: A 70-year-old man comes to the physician because of a rash for 7 days. Physical examination shows multiple 4- to 6-cm tense bullae filled with clear fluid over the inner aspects of the forearms, lower abdomen, groin, and thighs. Examination of a skin biopsy specimen shows a non-acantholytic blister with separation of the epidermis from the basement membrane. Serologic studies are most likely to show an autoantibody directed against which of the following?
additions.explanation: This patient has bullous pemphigoid: tense bullae in an older adult with a subepidermal, non-acantholytic blister. Bullous pemphigoid is caused by autoantibodies against hemidesmosomal proteins (BP180/BP230) that anchor basal keratinocytes to the basement membrane.
additions.subject: Dermatology

additions.text: A 32-year-old man has had generalized band-like headaches and dizziness almost every day for the past 6 months. Physical examination and CT scan of the head show no abnormalities. Which of the following additional findings in this patient is consistent with a diagnosis of hypochondriasis rather than undifferentiated somatoform disorder?
additions.explanation: Hypochondriasis is characterized by disproportionate fear or preoccupation with having a serious illness despite minimal objective findings. Frequent visits, depressive symptoms, chronicity, and a history of unexplained symptoms can occur in several somatoform presentations and are less specific than intense disease fear.
additions.subject: Psychiatry

options.text: Persistence of symptoms longer than 6 months
